i maintain the argument that you need to prepare for latent/unrealized demand

there are clearly large DA consumers which exist that do not use Ethereum DA because their usecase outstrips available supply

author: trent_vanepps

content: generally, if the average posture of core devs is "we dont need to increase" or "we'll wait until demand shows up to a certain level" we risk losing latent demand

author: cskiraly
content: I think the important part is to understand the undelying reasons. While I was not digging into this, I can imagine demand moving elsewhere because we are not signaling we would, or could, increase it.

content:
> I can imagine demand moving elsewhere because we are not signaling we would, or could, increase it.

you dont have to imagine the counterfactual 🙂 there are large DA consumers which currently do not use blobs or cannot use it for eg. payments usecases because there is not enough supply

content: I haven't heard anyone saying this

author: barnabasbusa
content: haven't heard from L2s either that they hate paying for blob data

author: trent_vanepps
content:
that's also a poor framing. no one is complaining about paying for blobs

but at a certain point, there is a cap on the total supply

author: cskiraly
content: I see lots of negative messages around this subject (no demand, no priority, not focus, etc.). My preferene would be to test higher and make sure what Barnabas said holds (I think it does), and then communicate that.

author: leobago
content: I don't think is a question about "we don't need" or "wait until demand arrives". The real question is whether the network can handle the pressure at a sustained high bandwidth level.

author: leobago
content: It is kind of equivalent to say to my kid, well you have no experience driving at 100km/h but here this bike that can go at 200km/h. Just in case you need it.

author: cskiraly
content: To be more specific, making sure we have the capacity when need arises requires networking changes. Until the attitude to networking improvements is "there is anyway no demand so there will be no demand till Hegota", we are just not giving good signs.

author: trent_vanepps
content:
if you've spoken with DA consumers recently, please forward to derek at ethlabs! he's putting together a blob survey. my conversations with blob consumers suggest they would like a clear projection of the future to plan around

> give us the actual capability to support payments use cases that require way more throughput.

https://x.com/jessepollak/status/2092321710846742760?s=20

author: trent_vanepps
content:
as a comparative frame: why are we increasing the gas limit 3.3X with glamsterdam? base fees are reasonably low lately

i assume it is because greater throughput to enable lower fees, even in congestion, is good consistent goal to have

the blob target/cap shouldn't be a threshold to hit, it should just be congestion pricing
